title: Researchers find coastal wetlands reduce storm damage
text: Scientists compared storm damage along 23 coastal regions after three major hurricanes. Areas with wide wetlands suffered less flooding than nearby developed shorelines. The wetlands slowed waves and absorbed surge before it reached homes. Researchers said the findings support restoring marshes before building larger seawalls. The team published its analysis on Tuesday. Local officials will use the results to review planned coastal defenses.
reference: Wide coastal wetlands reduced flooding by slowing waves and absorbing storm surge. Researchers say restoring marshes can complement seawalls.

title: New battery design charges faster and lasts longer
text: Engineers unveiled a battery prototype that charges in ten minutes. In laboratory tests it retained 90 percent of its capacity after 1,500 cycles. The design replaces a graphite electrode with a silicon-rich material. Researchers said production costs remain uncertain. The team plans to test larger cells with an automotive partner later this year. The results appeared in a peer-reviewed journal.
reference: A silicon-rich battery prototype charged in ten minutes and kept 90 percent of its capacity after 1,500 cycles. Production costs remain unknown.

title: City expands free evening bus service
text: The city will add hourly bus trips after 9 p.m. on six routes starting in June. Officials say the expansion follows a year-long pilot that increased night ridership by 28 percent. The service is funded by a two-year regional mobility grant. Transit unions said the schedule requires hiring 40 additional drivers. The council approved the plan in a 9-2 vote Monday. Riders can check new times on the transit agency website.
reference: The city approved hourly evening buses on six routes after a pilot increased night ridership 28 percent. The grant funds two years of service and requires hiring 40 more drivers.

title: Desert observatory captures comet debris trail
text: Astronomers at the Atacama observatory recorded the first detailed images of a comet debris trail breaking apart. The photographs show the trail fragmenting into more than a dozen pieces over six nights. Researchers believe solar radiation gradually loosened the icy chunks. The observations will help refine models of how comets decay near the sun. The team released the images through an open science portal. Further monitoring is planned during the comet's return in two years.
reference: Astronomers imaged a comet debris trail fragmenting into more than a dozen pieces over six nights. The data will refine models of how comets decay near the sun.

title: University library opens automated storage wing
text: The university opened an automated storage wing that holds two million volumes underground. Robotic cranes retrieve requested books and deliver them to a pickup desk within minutes. Librarians say the system frees the main hall for study space and exhibitions. The project took three years and cost 42 million dollars. Students can request materials through the library catalog. Staff received training to maintain the retrieval machinery.
reference: A robotic underground wing now stores two million volumes and fetches requests within minutes. The project frees main-hall space and cost 42 million dollars.

title: Farmers trial drought-resistant bean variety
text: Agricultural researchers distributed a drought-resistant bean variety to 300 farms across the dry corridor. Early harvests matched traditional yields while using 30 percent less water. The beans were bred through conventional cross-pollination over nine seasons. Farmers reported fewer losses during the irregular rainy season. Seed banks will store the variety for regional distribution next year. Researchers caution that soil quality still limits results in some areas.
reference: A conventionally bred bean matched traditional yields using 30 percent less water across 300 farms. Seed banks will distribute the variety regionally next year.

title: Transit agency pilots contactless fare cards
text: The transit agency began piloting contactless fare cards at 12 downtown stations. Riders can tap bank cards or phones instead of buying paper tickets. Early data shows boarding times improved by eight seconds per passenger. Officials plan to expand the system to all rail lines by autumn. Advocates asked for cash alternatives for unbanked riders. The agency said retail kiosks will top up reusable cards.
reference: Contactless tapping at 12 stations cut boarding times by eight seconds per rider. Expansion to all rail lines is planned, with cash kiosks for unbanked passengers.

title: Coastal city tests floating flood barriers
text: Engineers deployed inflatable flood barriers across a harbor channel to protect the old town. The barriers rise within an hour when storms push tides above the quay. A recent surge test held back water for two days without leaks. City planners estimate the system costs half as much as raising sea walls. Maintenance crews will inspect the anchors each season. Residents can track deployment alerts through the city website.
reference: Inflatable harbor barriers rise within an hour and held back a two-day surge without leaks. Planners estimate the system costs half as much as raising sea walls.

title: Museum returns ancient tablets to origin country
text: The museum formally returned 34 ancient clay tablets to the country where they were excavated. The tablets document trade records from a river valley civilization. Researchers there will digitize the collection for public study. The return follows a three-year review of acquisition records. Museum officials apologized for the 1960s purchases. A joint exhibition of reproductions opens next spring.
reference: The museum returned 34 clay tablets after a three-year acquisition review. The tablets will be digitized, with a joint exhibition of reproductions planned.

title: Startup orbits first debris-tracking satellite
text: A startup launched its first satellite dedicated to tracking small orbital debris. The spacecraft maps objects as small as one centimeter using laser ranging. Ground teams processed the first tracking data within a day of reaching orbit. Aviation authorities may use the catalog to adjust launch windows. The company plans a constellation of six satellites by 2028. Insurers expressed interest in risk models built from the data.
reference: A new satellite maps orbital debris as small as one centimeter using laser ranging. Six more satellites are planned by 2028 to support launch and insurance decisions.
